newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST - Cerebos interims seen weak.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Cerebos interims seen weak.

text.p: Singapore-based Cerebos Pacific Ltd is expected to unveil a sluggish set of half-time results next week, dragged down mainly by weak economies in Thailand and Australia, investment analysts said on Thursday.
The food group, which has most of its markets in the Asia-Pacific region, is expected to report its first half results for the six months ended March 31 1997 next Tuesday.
Analysts said Cerebos, which makes Brand's essence of chicken and other food products, would see slower profit growth, possibly slipping to single digits.
Cerebos has said it hopes to maintain double digit growth this fiscal year. Last year, it made net profits of Singapore $102.15 million (US$71.43 million), up 11 percent.
Analysts polled in Edinburgh Financial Publishing's Estimate Directory said they expected the group to make net profits of S$113.5 million for 1997.
"Cerebos is going to have a weak set of results. I am going for six to eight percent growth for the first half," Michael Ong, investment analyst with Soc-Gen Crosby Securities said.
Ong said sales in Thailand, a key market for Cerebos, had been slowing down sharply due to problems with the economy there.
Patrick Yau, investment analyst with Schroder Securities, said he expected growth of "near 10 percent" for the group.
"The problem is that the markets they are in are weak and not because their products are bad," he said.
Yau said he expected contributions from Australia and New Zealand, which contribute about 30 percent of group earnings, to continue to show a decline.
Cerebos sells a whole range of grocery products ranging from coffee and juices to salt and sauces.
The analysts said Asia, which accounts for about 70 percent of group profit, also had a difficult year.
Sales of Brands, Cerebos's flagship product, have been hit in the faltering Thailand market where it is regarded as a "luxury" food item.
Sales in China have not not taken off as expected due to credit problems with distributors there, said Yau.

Meanwhile, Cerebos's new acquisitions, like Woh Hup Food Industries which makes a range of Asian sauces, are also expected to be a drag on profits as they are being restructured, said an analyst with a European broking firm.
But despite the slower growth, Cerebos's balance sheet remains healthy with cash of about S$130 million which could be used for further acquisitions, the analysts said.
